title: Reading the Land
objective: After this level you can read elevation on a map and name landforms like plateaus, valleys and deltas.
summary: Heights are measured above sea level, and contour lines join points of equal height. Plateaus, valleys and deltas are three landforms to spot.

cards.headline: A flat sheet of paper can show you how steep a mountain is.
cards.body: No shading, no 3D glasses. Just a bunch of wiggly lines, if you know how to read them.

cards.headline: Every height starts at the sea
cards.body: Every height on a map needs a zero, and the usual zero is mean sea level. So when you hear that Mount Everest, the world's highest mountain, stands about 8,849 m tall, that means 8,849 m above the sea. Your hometown has a number like that, too. It's just less likely to be on a postcard.

cards.headline: Lines that never go up or down
cards.body: A topographic map draws contour lines, each one joining points at the same elevation. Walk along one and you'd never climb or descend. The trick is the spacing: lines bunched close together mean the ground rises fast, a steep slope. Lines spread far apart mean gentle ground. A cliff looks like a traffic jam of lines.

cards.headline: Three shapes to spot on the land

items.label: Plateau
points: Rises sharply on at least one side

items.label: Valley
points: Low land carved by water and ice
Rivers cut a V; glaciers grind a U

items.label: Delta
points: Flat, low land at a river's mouth
Built from sediment the slowing river drops
Named for the triangle-shaped Greek letter Δ

cards.headline: Land: readable
learned: Heights are measured above sea level
Contour lines join points of equal elevation
Close contours mean a steep slope
Plateaus, valleys and deltas are landforms to spot

questions.prompt: On a topographic map, what does a contour line connect?

options.label: Towns in the same time zone
options.rationale: Time zones aren't drawn with contours.

options.label: The fastest route between two points

questions.explanation: Each contour line joins points at the same height. Close lines mean steep ground.

questions.prompt: Why does a delta form at a river's mouth?

options.label: Glaciers push rock down to the coast
Waves pile sand up against cliffs
options.rationale: Deltas are built by the river itself.

options.label: The slowing river drops its sediment there
Plates push the land up into a plateau
options.rationale: A plateau is raised land, not a river deposit.

questions.explanation: As a river slows near its mouth, the sediment it carries settles out and builds flat, low land.

questions.prompt: Contour lines and Level 3's parallels are both lines on maps. What does a parallel join?

options.label: Points at the same distance north or south of the Equator
Points with the same clock time

questions.explanation: A parallel joins places at the same latitude; a contour joins places at the same height.
